pharm: Adsorbs to hydroxyapatite crystals in bone and inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption, lowering serum calcium and reducing pathologic bone turnover
quick: Moderate hypercalcemia 60-90 mg, severe 90 mg, single IV infusion over 2-24 h (never exceed 90 mg)
Not applicable (IV infusion); maintain vigorous saline hydration
Incorporated into bone; potential fetal harm - avoid unless clearly needed
Avoid; not known if excreted in milk and infant effects unknown
Renally excreted; do not exceed 90 mg, infuse over longer time, withhold if function deteriorates
No specific adjustment stated in labeling
Serum creatinine before each dose; calcium, phosphate, magnesium, potassium
summary: Pamidronate disodium is an intravenous bisphosphonate that inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. In conjunction with adequate saline hydration it is indicated for moderate to severe hypercalcemia of malignancy, and for moderate to severe Paget's disease of bone and osteolytic bone lesions (e.g. of multiple myeloma and breast cancer metastases). It is given as a slow single IV infusion; single doses must never exceed 90 mg because of the risk of significant renal deterioration.
indications: Moderate or severe hypercalcemia of malignancy (with adequate hydration)
Moderate to severe Paget's disease of bone
Osteolytic bone lesions of multiple myeloma and osteolytic bone metastases of breast cancer (per labeling)

dosage.d: 60 to 90 mg as a SINGLE dose IV infusion over 2 to 24 hours
dosage.t: Single dose; allow at least 7 days before considering retreatment
dosage.n: Longer infusions (>2 h) reduce renal toxicity risk; ensure vigorous saline hydration

dosage.d: 90 mg as a SINGLE dose IV infusion over 2 to 24 hours
dosage.t: Single dose; retreatment after >=7 days if calcium fails to normalize/remains elevated
dosage.n: Never exceed a single dose of 90 mg

dosage.d: 30 mg/day IV over 4 hours on 3 consecutive days (total 90 mg)
dosage.t: Retreatment with the same dose if clinically indicated on relapse
dosage.n: Effectiveness shown mainly with ALP >=3x upper limit of normal

admin: For intravenous infusion only after reconstitution and dilution; never give as a bolus
Reconstitute and dilute in 0.45% or 0.9% sodium chloride or 5% dextrose
Infuse slowly - single doses 60-90 mg over 2 to 24 hours (longer infusions reduce renal toxicity)
Maintain vigorous saline hydration to restore urine output to about 2 L/day; avoid overhydration in cardiac failure
Do not exceed a single dose of 90 mg; assess serum creatinine before each treatment
moa: The principal pharmacologic action of pamidronate is inhibition of bone resorption. It adsorbs to calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite) crystals in bone and may directly block dissolution of this mineral component; in vitro studies suggest inhibition of osteoclast activity also contributes. At doses used for hypercalcemia it inhibits bone resorption without inhibiting bone formation and mineralization, and inhibits the accelerated osteoclast-driven resorption induced by tumors.

absolute: Clinically significant hypersensitivity to pamidronate or other bisphosphonates
relative: Pre-existing renal insufficiency (use longer infusions, do not exceed 90 mg)
Patients with potential for cardiac failure (avoid overhydration)
History of thyroid surgery / hypoparathyroidism (predisposes to hypocalcemia)
Invasive dental procedures / poor oral hygiene (osteonecrosis of the jaw risk)

preg: Bisphosphonates such as pamidronate are incorporated into the bone matrix and gradually released over weeks to years, so there is potential for fetal harm, particularly skeletal effects, even from accumulated drug. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Use during pregnancy should be avoided unless the potential benefit clearly justifies the potential risk to the fetus; advise women of childbearing potential of the potential hazard.
lact: It is not known whether pamidronate is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during therapy.
renal: Pamidronate is excreted intact primarily by the kidney, so the risk of renal adverse reactions is greater with impaired renal function. Single doses must never exceed 90 mg, and longer infusion durations (>2 hours) reduce renal toxicity. Assess serum creatinine before each dose; in patients treated for bone metastases, withhold the dose if renal function has deteriorated and resume when it returns to baseline. Renal deterioration, progression to renal failure, dialysis, and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis have been reported.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is described in the labeling.

moderate: Other potentially nephrotoxic drugs - additive risk of renal deterioration
Loop diuretics - use only after correction of hypovolemia
Other bisphosphonates / calcium-lowering agents - additive risk of hypocalcemia
interactions.diagnostics: Transient hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia, hypomagnesemia and hypokalemia may be seen on laboratory testing

common: Transient fever (>=1 C rise 24-48 h after infusion)
Local injection-site reactions (redness, swelling, induration, pain)
serious: Deterioration of renal function progressing to renal failure
Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis with or without nephrotic syndrome
Osteonecrosis of the jaw (especially with dental procedures/cancer)
Atypical femoral fractures with long-term use
emergency: Severe symptomatic hypocalcemia with tetany / cardiac effects

monitoring: Serum calcium (corrected for albumin), phosphate, magnesium, potassium
Urine output and fluid status during hydration
Dental examination and oral hygiene (osteonecrosis of jaw)
counsel: This medicine is given by a slow drip into a vein, usually as a single dose
You may get a short-lived fever, flu-like aches, or soreness at the drip site in the first 1-2 days
Maintain good oral hygiene and tell your dentist you receive this medicine before any dental procedure
Report numbness, tingling, muscle cramps, reduced urine output, or eye pain/redness
Calcium and vitamin D supplements may be advised - follow your clinician's instructions
pk: Serum calcium begins to fall within 24-48 hours of infusion
Maximal calcium-lowering effect typically within several days
Not metabolized; biphasic skeletal retention - bound drug released over a very long period (terminal elimination from bone is prolonged)
Normocalcemia frequently maintained for ~7-14 days or longer after a single dose
Store at 20 to 25 C (68 to 77 F); controlled room temperature
pearls: Always pair pamidronate with vigorous saline hydration when treating hypercalcemia of malignancy
Never give a single dose above 90 mg and never as a bolus - renal failure and FSGS have occurred after single doses
Acute-phase reaction (fever, myalgia, flu-like symptoms) is common 24-48 h after the first dose and usually self-limited
Check serum creatinine before every dose; withhold in bone-metastasis patients if renal function deteriorates
Osteonecrosis of the jaw and atypical femoral fractures are class bisphosphonate risks - dental clearance before invasive procedures
missed: Not applicable - pamidronate is administered as a clinician-given intravenous infusion on a defined schedule, not self-administered. If a scheduled retreatment is delayed, the clinician determines timing based on serum calcium and renal function.
overdose: Overdose (reported with total doses of 225-300 mg over 2.5-4 days) causes symptomatic hypocalcemia that may require intravenous and/or oral calcium; high fever and transient hypotension have also been reported with single doses of about 285 mg. Treatment is supportive with short-term intravenous calcium for symptomatic hypocalcemia, and management of fever and hypotension (steroids have been used). There is no specific antidote.
